page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 vector extensions, alongside dedicated AES and SHA hardware encryption flags. The server contains no local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators, using networked block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-threaded computing capabilities. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 2532.0, complemented by top-tier single-core stress-ng performance of 3442.17 and high single-threaded throughput in data compression (37.65 GB/sec in gzip and 16.7 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression). Text processing tests also registered in the top decile. In contrast, multi-threaded operations position within the middle 50% baseline, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 9797.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 17535.04. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 48.64 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 26.09 GB/sec for uncached writes.

Application-level throughput reflects a balanced architecture, registering 14.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 26.51 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Small-model machine learning inference achieves 340.98 tokens per second during text generation, though prompt ingestion on medium 7B models drops to 30.28 tokens per second. The n4d-standard-8 offers consistent dedicated CPU execution without shared-core interference, making it suitable for general application servers, microservice backends, text parsing pipelines, and relational database hosting.

Multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth align within median industry baselines, handling 14.96 million Redis SET operations per second and 26.51 GB/sec of static web serving.
